title: Fix cache-replay token undercount causing billing credit churn after region failover
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Several customers reported unexpected invoice credits and then re-billing following a cross-region failover last week. Root cause analysis shows an edge case in our token accounting pipeline where cache-replayed requests that are retried across regions were excluded from per-request token tallies, producing undercounts that triggered manual reconciliation flows and customer-facing credits.

Scope & Impact: Affected traffic patterns include: - Hosted API requests routed through the smart router that experienced cross-region fallback (region failover and latency-based reroute). - Dedicated capacity customers with multi-region fallback enabled. - Private/VPC deployments that rely on our control-plane-assisted failover (customers using the automated failover knob). The issue produced underreported token usage for a subset (~0.3%) of requests during the failover window (2026-03-08 03:20 UTC to 2026-03-08 06:45 UTC). High-value customers with sustained traffic saw non-trivial credit adjustments after the nightly reconciliation job.

Technical details (initial findings): - Metering pipeline expects each request to have a canonical idempotency key (request_id) that is propagated from edge -> router -> runtime -> metering worker. - During cross-region replay, the router rewrites the request for failover and attaches an internal replay marker (X-RW-Region-Replay). In some code paths we generated a new request_id instead of preserving the original idempotency key. - Metering dedup/merge logic uses request_id + cache_hit flag to decide whether to emit token events. Replayed requests with a generated new id were classified as cache hits and skipped from metering emission, causing undercount. - The issue manifests differently by deployment type because Dedicated and Private use a different proxying path (internal proxy vs. hosted edge) which interacts with the router rewrite code in distinct ways; this explains why the customer impact profile varied.

Reproduction steps: 1) Simulate region failover in staging (us-west-2 -> eu-west-1) with continuous streaming chat sessions that rely on prefix-KV cache. 2) Force router-level replay with header X-RW-Inject-Replay: true. 3) Observe metering events emitted by the meter-frontend: requests where cache_replayed=true and request_id != original are missing token_emitted events. 4) Run nightly reconciliation simulation to confirm retroactive credit path is exercised.

Hypothesis: A missing preservation of the canonical request id in the router when performing cross-region replay is the root cause. Secondary contributing factors: metering dedup logic assumes idempotency is preserved, and the reconciliation job treats missing token events as negative adjustments when comparing request logs vs. billing aggregates.

Proposed fix and acceptance criteria: - Patch the smart-router to preserve the original request_id on replayed requests (minimal change, add preserve_request_id flag). - Harden metering pipeline: require both original_request_id and x-request-orig header as fallback for dedup, and add a reconcile-tolerance window metric. - Add integration tests that simulate region failover with replay to prevent regression. - Add monitoring and alerts: a synthetic that compares live token emission counts to proxied request counts and raises >0.5% drift alerts for 5m. Acceptance: replayed requests must produce token_emitted events in staging and canary; nightly reconciliation should no longer generate retroactive credits for simulated failovers.

Mitigations taken: - Immediately disabled cross-region KV cache-replay for affected clusters for 24 hours (rollback via feature flag). - Issued temporary manual credits to customers with visible variance while we investigate (cust-svcs-ops ticket linked). - Elevated trace sampling for router->runtime->metering paths to 100% for the failover window.

Work items: - ENG: implement router patch and unit tests (Ravi) - ENG: update metering dedup logic and add integration test harness (Santiago) - ENG/Infra: run reconciliation dry-run against write-ahead logs for 2026-03-08 window (Mina) - ENG/Support: prepare customer comms and detailed per-customer variance report (Elena) - PM: coordinate customer outreach and credits policy (Jordan)

References & artifacts: - Confluence incident doc: https://confluence.redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-03-cache-replay
- Repro harness & test plan: https://drive.redwood.internal/drive/folders/metering-replay-tests-2026
- Patch PR (in progress): https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/4821
- Metering pipeline draft fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/2380
- Customer variance dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/metering/variance-2026-03

Notes: We need to be careful with the reconciliation path. Several tooling teams automatically issue credits based on the reconciliation diff — until the patch is deployed and reconciliation logic is adjusted we should keep automated credit flows paused for the impacted window to avoid churn.
